name: Kumospace
tagline: Host a lightweight spatial room for a small team without production media guarantees

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 5 registered members; 1 floor; unlimited rooms; up to 50 concurrent guests; each guest may use the workspace up to 4 hours/week

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Minimum 5 paid members; unlimited floors and rooms; up to 50 concurrent guests; recording and analytics
tiers.notes: Billed annually; minimum annualized base is 5 × $16 = $80/month. Annual billing saves 20%; exact month-to-month rate was not exposed.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited guests plus custom security, onboarding and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: 5 registered members; 1 floor; unlimited rooms; 50 concurrent guests; each guest limited to 4 hours/week
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-20% annually); public Business price is $16/member/month billed annually; 5-seat minimum
pricing.hiddenCosts: Business has a 5-paid-member minimum. A 14-day paid-plan trial can auto-convert to a subscription; added members are prorated, while removals generally affect the next invoice.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Kumospace, host a lightweight spatial room for a small team without production media guarantees. The hard boundary is real-time video infrastructure, office presence, moderation, analytics, and support, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a lightweight spatial room for a small team without production media guarantees, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: real-time video infrastructure, office presence, moderation, analytics, and support
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Kumospace because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Cosmos Free
alternatives.desc: Four concurrent people get an always-on spatial office, chat and unlimited calls.

facts.install: Hosted signup in the browser, with optional native desktop and mobile apps
facts.engines: Built-in transcription and AI meeting summaries; the provider and model are not disclosed in public first-party documentation
facts.dataFormat: Account, messages and files live in Cosmos's cloud; calls are transmitted encrypted, while user-started recordings are stored on Cosmos servers and some recording or message data is handled by US processors
facts.gapVsPaid: The four-person concurrent cap and lighter office customization, administration, chat and integrations make it a smaller team workspace than Kumospace.

alternatives.name: flat.social Free
alternatives.desc: Five people, unlimited sessions and custom rooms; enough office for a genuinely small team.

facts.install: Hosted browser signup; guests join by link
facts.dataFormat: Accounts, room definitions and shared content live in flat.social's hosted service; device and usage data is collected by the service, while live media is handled in the browser
facts.gapVsPaid: Its five-person cap and simpler office management, chat integrations and whiteboard or document workflow are the main step down.

alternatives.name: Kumospace Free
alternatives.desc: The actual product is free for five registered members, with customizable rooms and basic chat intact.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser; desktop and mobile apps are optional
facts.dataFormat: Rooms, chat and files live in Kumospace's cloud; audio and video is relayed through Daily or Agora and is not persistently recorded by Kumospace
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan is the same product, but it stops at five registered members, one floor and a public space, without paid security, admin, integrations or advanced analytics.

alternatives.name: SpatialChat Free
alternatives.desc: Twelve people fit, but only for two hours a day; permanent free does not mean permanently open.

facts.install: Hosted browser signup; guests join by link
facts.dataFormat: Spaces, uploaded files and account data live in SpatialChat's hosted service; calls occur in the browser
facts.gapVsPaid: The two-hour daily limit is a deal-breaker for an always-on team office.

alternatives.name: WorkAdventure Free
alternatives.desc: A pixel office for ten simultaneous people; less boardroom, more tiny RPG.

facts.install: Create a hosted space in the browser, or self-host with Docker Compose or the Helm and Kubernetes stack
facts.engines: Calls can use Jitsi or LiveKit; optional virtual-agent bots can connect to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI
facts.dataFormat: Hosted maps and account or room data live on WorkAdventure's EU service; self-hosted maps live on persistent volumes or S3-compatible storage, with original map sources kept separately by the user
facts.gapVsPaid: Its pixel-world aesthetic and Tiled-based map editing are less boardroom-friendly and harder for nontechnical office admins than Kumospace.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is clean; self-hosting needs Docker or Helm, domain/TLS, TURN and conferencing services, and serious map customization often starts in Tiled

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Business plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Kumospace in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a lightweight spatial room for a small team without production media guarantees, organize discussion into channels or topics, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
